name: Xiongnu
summary: A confederation of nomadic peoples on the Mongolian steppe that challenged Han China for centuries. It is a possible ancestor of the Huns.

location.value: Mongolia, eastern Kazakhstan and southern Siberia.

terrain.value: Grassland steppe, mountains and the Gobi Desert.

climate.value: Cold, dry steppe with harsh winters.

resources.value: Pasture for horses, sheep and cattle; iron.

disasters.value: Harsh winters (zud) killed livestock and caused famine.

urbanisation.value: Mostly nomadic, with some fortified settlements and royal tombs.

migration.value: Split into northern and southern groups in 48 CE; many were later resettled inside Han borders.

economicBase.value: Herding, raiding and tribute from Han China.
economicBase.source: Wikipedia: Xiongnu (checked 6 Nov 2026); Barfield, The Perilous Frontier (1989)

tradeRoutes.value: Received Han silk through tribute and border markets; controlled parts of the early Silk Road.

wealth.value: No estimate is possible for this period.

moneyAndTax.value: No coinage; wealth was counted in livestock and tribute.

inequality.value: The chanyu and aristocratic clans led; ordinary herders served as soldiers.

governmentType.value: A tribal confederation under a supreme ruler, the chanyu.
governmentType.source: Wikipedia: Xiongnu (checked 6 Nov 2026); Barfield, The Perilous Frontier (1989)

succession.value: Usually within the ruling Luanti clan, often disputed.

institutions.value: Left and right wings under senior princes, a model later used by other steppe empires.

stability.value: Civil wars between rival chanyu from 57 BCE.

eliteConflict.value: Rival princes fought over the succession.

armyAndTech.value: Mounted archers able to field very large cavalry armies.
armyAndTech.source: Wikipedia: Xiongnu (checked 6 Nov 2026); Barfield, The Perilous Frontier (1989)

majorWars.value: Battle of Baideng (200 BCE); long wars with Han China (from 133 BCE).
majorWars.source: Wikipedia: Xiongnu (checked 6 Nov 2026); Barfield, The Perilous Frontier (1989)

territoryChange.value: Defeated the Yuezhi and dominated the eastern steppe.
territoryChange.source: Wikipedia: Xiongnu (checked 6 Nov 2026); Barfield, The Perilous Frontier (1989)

alliancesRivals.value: Rivals: Han China, the Yuezhi and the Xianbei.
alliancesRivals.source: Wikipedia: Xiongnu (checked 6 Nov 2026); Barfield, The Perilous Frontier (1989)

scienceEducation.value: No writing of their own is known.

openness.value: A multi-ethnic confederation that traded with China and Central Asia.
openness.source: Wikipedia: Xiongnu (checked 6 Nov 2026); Barfield, The Perilous Frontier (1989)

religion.source: Wikipedia: Xiongnu (checked 6 Nov 2026); Barfield, The Perilous Frontier (1989)

languageWriting.value: Language is unknown; links to Turkic, Iranian, Mongolic, Yeniseian and other families are debated.

artsArchitecture.value: Bronze belt plaques and animal-style art; rich royal tombs at Noin-Ula.

neighbours.value: Han China, the Yuezhi and the Xianbei.
neighbours.source: Wikipedia: Xiongnu (checked 6 Nov 2026); Barfield, The Perilous Frontier (1989)

ideasReligions.value: Steppe traditions passed to later nomadic empires.

peakPeriod.value: Under Modu Chanyu (209–174 BCE), when the Han paid tribute.

declineSignals.value: Long wars with the Han and civil wars.
declineSignals.source: Wikipedia: Xiongnu (checked 6 Nov 2026); Barfield, The Perilous Frontier (1989)

outcome.value: Defeated by the Han; split. End date differs (late 1st century CE or 2nd century CE).

sources.value: Chinese records (Sima Qian) and archaeology. Checked against Wikipedia (“Xiongnu”).

overallCertainty.value: Low to medium. Known mostly from Chinese sources.

knownFor.label: Mounted archers
knownFor.note: Steppe horse archers who raided the Han frontier.

knownFor.label: Animal-style bronzes
knownFor.note: Bronze belt plaques with fighting animals.
